analysis.summary: Portugal and Spain meet in an Iberian heavyweight clash at AT&T Stadium in the Round of 16. Spain arrive as the tournament's most complete side, unbeaten in 34 matches and the only team yet to concede a goal across four World Cup games, while Portugal have been inconsistent and needed a Ramos stoppage-time winner to edge past Croatia in the Round of 32. Spain are clear favorites on form, but Portugal's 2024-25 Nations League Final victory over this same opponent on penalties adds genuine uncertainty should the game go deep.
analysis.home_form: Portugal finished second in Group K (5 pts) after a 1-1 draw with DR Congo, a 5-0 win over Uzbekistan (Ronaldo scored twice), and a 0-0 draw with Colombia. In the Round of 32 on July 3 they trailed Croatia 0-1 before Ronaldo converted a penalty in the 68th minute and Ramos headed a winner in the 90th+4 to escape 2-1. Portugal have averaged only 3.8 shots on target per game — below the level expected of a top-eight contender — and despite controlling 61% possession across five matches their attack has been ponderous.
analysis.away_form: Spain topped Group H with 7 points: 0-0 vs Cape Verde, 4-0 vs Saudi Arabia, 1-0 vs Uruguay, then dismantled Austria 3-0 in the Round of 32 on July 2 (Oyarzabal brace, Porro). They have kept four consecutive clean sheets — the first time Spain have done so across four World Cup games — and are unbeaten across their last 34 competitive matches. Joint-top scorer Mikel Oyarzabal has four tournament goals; Lamine Yamal supplies consistent width from the right.
analysis.h2h: Spain lead the all-time series 17 wins to 6 wins for Portugal (18 draws) across 41 meetings. In four recent competitive meetings the average has been 3.3 goals per game. Memorable encounters include the 2018 World Cup 3-3 (Ronaldo hat-trick) and the 2024-25 UEFA Nations League Final where Portugal won on penalties after a 1-1 draw, with Ronaldo scoring the 61st-minute equalizer. Ronaldo has scored four career goals against Spain, joint-most of any player. Recent competitive head-to-head is effectively balanced.
injuries_news: Spain: Nico Williams (right adductor injury suffered vs Uruguay) did not start vs Austria but was named on the bench; he is reported to be trending toward available for this match and may feature.
Spain: Yeremy Pino (collar bone injury) is expected to miss the remainder of the tournament.
Portugal: No confirmed injuries or suspensions entering this fixture.
key_factors: Spain's tournament-best defensive record — four clean sheets with no goals conceded — will test Portugal's underwhelming attack (3.8 shots on target per game).

Cristiano Ronaldo's personal motivation ('this will be my last World Cup') and his four career goals against Spain introduce an emotional wildcard; he scored the late equalizer in the 2024-25 Nations League Final vs this opponent.
Both teams average over 60% possession: the midfield duel between Rodri/Pedri and Vitinha/Joao Neves/Bruno Fernandes is likely to define attacking opportunities.
Potential return of Nico Williams would give Spain an additional width option against Portugal's right side (Cancelo) and increase their goal threat.
Rest advantage is negligible: Spain played July 2, Portugal July 3 — both have three days' recovery.
AT&T Stadium in Arlington is a neutral indoor venue with no altitude or weather concern; conditions are equal.
Portugal beat Spain on penalties in the 2024-25 Nations League Final — if this match goes to a shootout, Portugal's recent penalty record is an asset.
